problem: Latent diffusion models achieve poor quality-compute trade-offs because fixed tokenizers limit adaptive compression and variable-length tokenization breaks representational alignment across different compression ratios.
approach: A novel variable-length tokenizer that merges similar tokens rather than truncating sequences, with learnable global merging that is data-independent to ensure compatibility during generation.
contribution: Achieves superior gFID-compute trade-off on ImageNet 256×256 compared to prior variable-length tokenizer methods.

problem: Reinforcement learning on LLMs is limited to the model's own distribution, preventing acquisition of reasoning skills beyond initial knowledge.
approach: DALSA framework that adaptively assigns supervised fine-tuning to samples beyond model knowledge, reinforcement learning to boundary samples, and discards well-learned samples, using learnable strategy allocation based on training dynamics.
contribution: Consistently outperforms baselines on 10 LLMs (1.5B-70B) across various tasks under full and parameter-efficient fine-tuning.

problem: Layout-to-image models struggle with inter-object occlusion because overlapping bounding boxes lack explicit occlusion information, creating ambiguity in intersection regions.
approach: OcclusionFormer, a diffusion transformer that explicitly models Z-order priority by decoupling instances and compositing via volume rendering, with a queried alignment loss for fine-grained spatial precision.
contribution: Reduces ambiguity in overlapping regions and enforces correct occlusion dependencies with substantial accuracy gains.

problem: Existing RLHF methods are non-robust and degrade when downstream task distributions differ significantly from the preference dataset used for fine-tuning.
approach: Distributionally robust optimization formulation of reward-based RLHF and reward-free DPO, using minibatch gradient descent algorithms with theoretical convergence guarantees.
contribution: Robust training improves reward model accuracy and markedly on reasoning tasks, with better out-of-distribution performance than standard methods.

problem: Scientific machine learning models exhibit inconsistent behavior across hyperparameter settings, with distinct failure modes that conventional loss-landscape metrics miss.
approach: A regime-aware diagnostic framework that jointly analyzes performance, training dynamics, and loss-landscape geometry to identify and characterize distinct training regimes.
contribution: Identifies a consistent three-regime structure across standard SciML models with regime-specific optimization effectiveness, revealing fine-grained failure modes.

problem: Synthetic data from diffusion models has untapped potential for image segmentation, with factors governing effectiveness remaining underexplored.
approach: Systematic analysis of diffusion-generated synthetic images identifies that dense scene composition and fine instance fidelity drive segmentation benefits, leading to SENSE framework for flexible synthetic data generation.
contribution: SENSE is model-agnostic, compatible with diverse architectures, and substantially enhances segmentation performance on Cityscapes, COCO, and ADE20K.

problem: Cross-subject generalization in biomedical time-series fails because subject-specific variability (magnitude/phase shifts in frequency components) is not explicitly modeled.
approach: BioFormer with Frequency-Band Alignment Module (FBAM) that generates band-wise modulation factors to align spectral structure, paired with Sample Conditional Layer Normalization.
contribution: Outperforms 12 baselines with absolute F1-score improvements of 6% on six biomedical datasets.

problem: Iterative image editing with diffusion transformers wastes substantial computation because the model processes all tokens uniformly even when most regions are unchanged by the instruction.
approach: CacheEdit framework with Adaptive Activation Cache that exploits early-step sensitivity to detect invariant tokens and reuses their cached activations across sampling steps.
contribution: Achieves up to 2.5× end-to-end acceleration while improving instruction-following and structural consistency.

problem: Decision-time planning in model-based RL requires state representations that support local cost computation while preserving long-horizon structure, which typical representations fail to achieve.
approach: ALPS, a hierarchical planning algorithm that leverages Laplacian representations to capture state-space distances at multiple time scales and naturally decompose problems into subgoals.
contribution: Outperforms baselines on offline goal-conditioned RL tasks from OGBench, a benchmark previously dominated by model-free methods.

problem: AI labor markets will operate at much higher frequency than human labor markets, yet frameworks to understand strategic behavior and microeconomic properties of AI-only markets are missing.
approach: AI-Work, a simulated gig economy where LLM agents compete for jobs and develop skills, examining three domains of strategic capabilities: metacognition, competitive awareness, and long-horizon planning.
contribution: Demonstrates that agents with metacognition, competitive awareness, and strategic planning consistently achieve higher profits and market share than competing agents.

problem: Long-video question-answering with fixed token budgets struggles to balance temporal localization and high-quality frame processing while providing interpretable answers.
approach: Video-in-the-Loop (ViTL), a two-stage framework that first localizes question-relevant intervals with low-fps skim, then answers via span-aware token reallocation at higher effective frame rate with interleaved output.
contribution: Attains up to 8.6% improvement with 50% less frame input on long-video QA and temporal grounding benchmarks.

problem: Time series forecasting with transformers assumes uniform temporal progression via positional encodings, but real-world systems exhibit time-warped dynamics where the effective flow of time decouples from the sampling index.
approach: StretchTime with Symplectic Positional Embeddings (SyPE) derived from Hamiltonian mechanics that extend rotary embeddings to capture non-affine temporal warping via an adaptive warp module.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on standard benchmarks with superior robustness on non-stationary temporal dynamics.

problem: Understanding LLM personality relies on simplified self-reports and heuristic prompting without behavioral validation, obscuring dissociation between self-reported traits and actual behavior.
approach: Systematic characterization of LLM personality across three dimensions: trait emergence during training, predictive validity of self-reported traits in behavioral tasks, and impact of persona injection interventions.
contribution: Reveals that instructional alignment stabilizes trait expression but self-reported traits do not reliably predict behavior, with persona injection steering self-reports but not actual behavior.

problem: Mixture-of-Experts architectures face an inherent trade-off between expert granularity and hardware execution efficiency, limiting practical scaling.
approach: OmniMoE, a system-algorithm co-designed MoE with vector-level Atomic Experts, using a Cartesian Product Router to reduce routing complexity from O(N) to O(√N) and Expert-Centric Scheduling for efficient execution.
contribution: Achieves 50.9% zero-shot accuracy on seven benchmarks with 10.9× speedup (73ms to 6.7ms latency) compared to fine-grained baselines.

problem: Quantized neural networks retain high-precision partial sums during accumulation, resulting in significant energy overhead on NPU accelerators.
approach: PsumQuant, a post-training input-aware quantization that predicts partial sum scales on-the-fly by leveraging input activation crest factors with a learnable scale predictor.
contribution: Compresses partial sum precision to 8-bit with only 1% accuracy drop on ResNet-18 and 0.04 perplexity increase on Llama-3.1, achieving 45% total energy reduction.

problem: HD map construction via DETR-based detection uses independent learnable queries with predominantly local perspective, neglecting inherent global map structure.
approach: MapGR architecture with Global Representation Learning module encouraging query distribution alignment via holistic segmentation, and Global Representation Guidance module providing each query with explicit global contextual information.
contribution: Demonstrates substantial improvements in mean Average Precision on nuScenes and Argoverse2 datasets compared to leading baselines.

problem: LLM personality control via fine-tuning is resource-intensive, requiring expensive data collection and distinct model training for each target personality.
approach: Inference-time activation steering using iteratively trained probes on residual streams that function as modular, reusable primitives for synthesizing complex personality profiles via coefficient adjustment.
contribution: Effectively modulates holistic personality profiles without updating base model parameters, validated via LLM-as-a-judge framework and Big Five inventory.

problem: Unified Foundation Models generating interleaved text and images may produce visual content as auxiliary output rather than grounded evidence, with functional dependence between modalities unclear.
approach: UFO benchmark evaluating whether Unified Foundation Models generate and use image and text cues as evidence across three state-transition regimes: state determination, reconstruction, and augmentation.
contribution: Reveals significant modality gap where models achieve high prediction accuracy despite limited visual influence on decisions, indicating reliance on textual shortcuts.

problem: Constrained diffusion models for scientific applications struggle with costly projections onto nonconvex feasible sets and high simulation costs for mixing.
approach: Unified framework for constrained diffusion on nonconvex feasible sets using a computationally efficient landing mechanism replacing projections, with underdamped dynamics for accelerated mixing.
contribution: Reduces function evaluations and memory usage while preserving sample quality on benchmarks with equality and mixed constraints.

problem: Theoretical understanding of transformer-based diffusion models remains limited, with no convergence analysis for training despite strong empirical performance.
approach: Convergence analysis for transformer-based DDPM training on multi-token Gaussian mixture data, showing self-attention implements mean denoising approximating the MMSE estimator.
contribution: Quantifies required tokens per data point and training iterations for global convergence toward Bayes optimal risk of the denoising objective.

problem: Machine unlearning with (ε,δ)-guarantees requires formal assurances but existing first-order methods either ignore forget set gradients or provide no formal guarantees.
approach: Variance-Reduced Unlearning (VRU), the first first-order algorithm that directly includes forget set gradients while provably satisfying (ε,δ)-unlearning with improved convergence rates.
contribution: Achieves strictly improved rates with better dependence on achieved error, asymptotically outperforming methods that ignore the forget set in low-error regime.

problem: Training prompt design for fine-tuning is largely unexplored; semantically equivalent prompts are assumed equivalent but actually induce drastically different cross-task generalization impacts.
approach: State-Adaptive Prompt Optimization (SAPO) that dynamically adjusts task formulation during training, identifying superior prompts via task loss prior to learning and optimizing over prompt selection.
contribution: Significantly mitigates catastrophic forgetting while improving generalization, achieving substantial performance gains over state-of-the-art methods.

problem: Federated parameter-efficient fine-tuning is vulnerable to backdoor poisoning when privacy constraints prevent inspection of real-valued updates from clients.
approach: IndexGuard, an unsupervised index-only vetting primitive where clients send only Top-K salient update indices, with server-side overlap geometry analysis to cluster clients and filter cohesion outliers.
contribution: Provides end-to-end backdoor mitigation preserving clean accuracy while achieving performance comparable to centralized methods.

problem: Medical vision-language models optimize linguistic fluency via RL rather than clinical correctness, causing Evaluation Hallucinations that lead to diagnostic errors on 3D CT analysis.
approach: Trajectory-Integral Feedback GRPO (TIF-GRPO) integrating control-theoretic principles into policy optimization, formulating clinical reasoning as pseudo-temporal trajectory with anatomy-aware reward regulation.
contribution: Significantly enhances abnormality detection and clinical faithfulness on 3D CT benchmarks by penalizing persistent omissions as cumulative state errors.

problem: AI assistants correct suboptimal human actions behaviorally, but long-term improvement requires addressing underlying misconceptions driving repeated mistakes.
approach: SENSEI framework that infers user misconceptions from interaction behavior via structured knowledge representation, providing targeted minimal suggestions to correct misconception sources.
contribution: Demonstrates zero-shot compositional generalization disentangling multiple overlapping misconceptions, with user study showing effective guidance that corrects 90% of student misconceptions.

problem: Reward model evaluation focuses on preference perception accuracy in given scenarios, obscuring critical vulnerabilities under real-world perturbations and conditional reliability.
approach: Reward Auditor, a hypothesis-testing framework using scientific auditing to assess RM suitability (conditional reliability under perturbations) via distribution degradation of RM confidence.
contribution: Quantifies statistical significance and effect size of RM vulnerabilities across diverse real-world scenarios, enabling inference of both certainty and severity.

problem: Surrogates for deformable solids under nonlinear elasticity and plasticity remain underexplored due to challenges in capturing transient behavior and nonlinear effects.
approach: Multigrid graph neural network coupling encoder-processor-decoder with physics-informed coarsening that scores nodes via residual-based local physical activity to preferentially retain high strain/stress regions.
contribution: Consistent accuracy gains and improved rollout stability on datasets covering linear, nonlinear, and transient regimes compared to standard sampling baselines.

problem: Weak-to-strong generalization requires identifying which weak labels are reliable enough to train a strong student when reliable labels are scarce.
approach: Trust functions that assign scalar trust scores to weak labels and filter weak supervision, enabling iterative weak-to-strong chains that compound gains by reusing students as next teachers.
contribution: Achieves near-lossless weak-to-strong generalization matching and sometimes surpassing ground-truth supervision, with implicit easy-first curriculum and more coherent gradient updates.

problem: Learning systems excel at interpolation but struggle to generalize to unseen tasks outside the training distribution's support, failing even on simple task parameter extrapolation.
approach: Relational Task Extrapolator (RTE) learning how tasks transform into one another by decomposing target tasks into known anchor tasks and learned transformations relating anchors to unseen targets.
contribution: Substantially outperforms existing approaches on parameter extrapolation, length extrapolation, and compositional extrapolation across function and sequence prediction.

problem: Urban wind flow reconstruction from sparse sensor data is challenging for neural network baselines and classical data assimilation methods.
approach: GenDA, a generative data assimilation framework using multiscale graph-based diffusion with classifier-free guidance where unconditional branch learns geometry-aware flow prior and sensor-conditioned branch injects observational constraints.
contribution: Reduces relative root-mean-square error by 25-57% and increases structural similarity by 23-33% compared to GNN baselines and classical methods on complex urban Reynolds-averaged Navier-Stokes simulations.

problem: Divergence estimation via density-ratio methods is challenging and computationally expensive.
approach: Rank-statistic approximation of f-divergences working directly with distribution of ranks, mapping mismatch between distributions to rank histograms and measuring deviation via discrete f-divergence.
contribution: Produces lower-bound estimates that are monotone in resolution parameter K with quantitative convergence rates, supporting sliced variants for high-dimensional data.

problem: Document parsing pipelines rely on complex Crop-OCR-Merge cascades to handle high-resolution inputs, introducing error propagation and complexity.
approach: OvisOCR, a lightweight end-to-end MLLM for document parsing that directly maps full-page visual signals to structured Markdown, using category-specific reward mechanisms for diverse document constituents.
contribution: Achieves top-tier performance on OmniDocBench across all aspects, demonstrating that compact E2E models can surpass specialized and general methods while eliminating error propagation.

problem: Overparameterized networks show good generalization attributed to implicit biases like norm minimization and low sharpness, but their interaction and joint contribution to generalization remains unclear.
approach: Analysis of implicit regularization trade-off between parameter norm and model sharpness across learning rates, proving neither bias alone minimizes generalization error for diagonal linear networks.
contribution: Demonstrates that learning rate interpolates between norm and sharpness biases, requiring broader view of implicit regularization capturing dynamic trade-off.

problem: The rent-or-buy problem for online trip planning has a competitive ratio of 2 with best deterministic algorithms, but predictability via offline samples is unexplored.
approach: Learning-augmented approach leveraging offline samples of trips to improve competitive ratio from 2 to 3/2, with further improvement under additional conditions.
contribution: Even sparse samples significantly improve competitive ratio, with theoretical bounds verified via numerical simulations across natural input classes.

problem: Deep lung cancer risk prediction models like Sybil lack causal verification despite extensive clinical validation, obscuring actual reasoning mechanisms critical before deployment.
approach: S(H)NAP, a model-agnostic auditing framework constructing generative interventional attributions via realistic 3D diffusion bridge modeling to systematically modify anatomical features and isolate causal contributions.
contribution: First interventional audit of Sybil reveals expert-like behavior in differentiating nodules but critical failure modes including sensitivity to unjustified artifacts and radial bias.

problem: Strategic agents gaming algorithmic systems assume fixed manipulation costs, but real costs evolve and depend on past algorithmic decisions, creating temporal dependencies.
approach: Two-stage robust optimization framework with decision-dependent uncertainty set capturing how today's decisions influence tomorrow's manipulation costs.
contribution: Awareness of policy-dependent costs reduces uncertainty and better curtails gaming of algorithmic systems over time compared to fixed-cost models.

problem: Multi-token prediction for speedup requires balancing expressiveness via joint token distributions against latency from sequential generation.
approach: MTPC framework using probabilistic circuits to explore different ways to encode joint distributions over future tokens, generalizing mixture models and hidden Markov models.
contribution: When combined with speculative decoding, substantially speeds up generation compared to independence-assumption MTP while retaining verifier LLM performance.

problem: Existing concept unlearning in diffusion models uses MSE loss (KL divergence for Gaussians), but impact of other f-divergences on unlearning efficacy and generative fidelity trade-off is unknown.
approach: Unified framework generalizing unlearning objective to any f-divergence, with min-max objective for divergences lacking closed-form, analyzing gradient magnitude and convergence properties.
contribution: Shows Hellinger closed-form instance consistently dominates MSE across scenarios, offering flexible paradigm for selecting optimal divergence based on application goals.

problem: Cyclic peptide modeling is challenging because ring-shaped conformations are diverse and cannot be captured by deterministic models derived from linear peptide folding.
approach: MuCO (Multi-stage Conformation Optimization), a generative method modeling cyclic peptide conformation distribution via three-stage decoupling: topology-aware backbone design, generative side-chain packing, and physics-aware all-atom optimization.
contribution: Significantly outperforms state-of-the-art on CPSea dataset in physical stability, structural diversity, secondary structure recovery, and computational efficiency.

problem: Vision-language models excel at reasoning but grounding predictions into precise robot actions remains challenging due to entanglement of reasoning and action generation.
approach: Generalizable Action Expert (GAE), a task-agnostic model converting sparse geometric plans (3D waypoints from VLM) into dense robot actions, pretrained on 150k trajectories and combined with VLM via lightweight fine-tuning.
contribution: Achieves strong performance and generalization across diverse visual domains, camera viewpoints, and natural language instructions with action-geometry decoupling.
